entities.summary: Violet Lucille Fletcher was an American screenwriter of film, radio and television. Her credits include The Hitch-Hiker, an original radio play written for Orson Welles and adapted for a notable episode of The Twilight Zone television series. Lucille Fletcher also wrote Sorry, Wrong Number, one of the most celebrated plays in the history of American radio, which she adapted and expanded for the 1948 film noir classic of the same name. Married to composer Bernard Herrmann in 1939, she wrote the libretto for his opera Wuthering Heights, which he began in 1943 and completed in 1951, after their divorce.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lucille Fletcher's radio play 'Sorry, Wrong Number' is considered one of the most celebrated plays in the history of American radio, with over 2 million listeners tuning in for its broadcast in 1943. Her work also influenced the development of film noir, as her 1948 screenplay adaptation was a major factor in the genre's success.
